controls.label: Thermal glow
controls.qualification: Black-body color at its measured dayside temperature, 1,992 K. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of WASP-79 b's heat: a black body at the dayside brightness temperature measured in secondary eclipse at 3.6 µm (Spitzer IRAC). Its star lights the day side; the night side is not measured. Reflected starlight is not included.

charts.alt: The orbits of Montuno's planets in this map from above, to scale, with WASP-79 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

WASP-79 b's transmission spectrum: the fraction of starlight the planet blocks as it crosses its star, larger where its atmosphere absorbs. 26 measured bins from Sotzen et al. 2020 (Magellan II Landon Clay Telescope, LDSS-3C; Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, TESS CCD Array; Hubble Space Telescope satellite, Wide Field Camera 3; Spitzer Space Telescope satellite, Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)), as the NASA Exoplanet Archive lists them. Horizontal bars are wavelength bins; vertical bars are the published 1-sigma errors.

WASP-79 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (32, 106, 107) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 170634116, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 15-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
